locales.summary: Chiang Mai is still the easiest place in Asia to settle in for months: fibre, coworking, mountain cafes and Thai food at very low cost, with a large long-stay community. The catch for a remote worker is practical: a tight rental market since the 2021 Tajogaite eruption, a small nomad scene, no verified coworking, and serious hospital care that can mean a transfer to Tenerife.

entry.summary: Spain-wide rules apply (La Palma is in Schengen). Telework visa for remote workers employed by or freelancing for non-Spanish companies: funds of 200% of the monthly minimum wage (SMI; check the current euro figure with the consulate), a degree or 3 years' relevant experience, a clean record; Spanish clients limited to 20% of activity (not applicable to EU citizens). The visa is valid 1 year; people already legally in Spain can apply for a residence permit of up to 3 years. EU citizens need no visa. US and UK passport holders get 90 days in any 180 across Schengen, shared with other Schengen countries. Canary Islands use IGIC instead of mainland VAT; Spanish tax residency applies from 183 days.

locales.caveats: Thin data: (1) AEMET's published normals page for La Palma Aeropuerto only shows 1981-2010, not 1991-2020; the airport is on the east coast at 33 m, so figures are a proxy for Los Llanos (about 340 m, west). No verified west-side normals; expect the west to be sunnier and drier in winter but a few degrees cooler inland. (2) Rent: portal figures conflict (Fotocasa EUR 440 average for Nov 2025 and 15.40 EUR/m2 in Nov 2026; RealAdvisor median EUR 911); idealista blocked fetching, no real 1-bed furnished listings were confirmed; the cost range is an estimate. (3) Housing: post-eruption shortage and 2026 protests reported; Canary holiday-let law (Ley 6/2025, in force 13 Dec 2025) and later amendments reportedly affect La Palma, details unverified. (4) Puerto Naos/La Bombilla: access is gradually reopening in phases by CO2 level (463 homes authorized in Puerto Naos and 3 in La Bombilla as of April 2024; 2026 reports mention further approvals, 42 businesses reopened in April 2026 and gas-extraction systems being installed); it is not fully open, so do not plan to live there. (5) Air quality PM2.5 and municipality fibre coverage were not found; national fibre coverage is about 96% of homes and 5G is widespread per the 2026 ministry report, but La Palma coverage is uneven. (6) Calima: AEMET and CSIC sources say intense episodes concentrate in winter; frequency figures vary by study. (7) Flights (Aena, Nov 2026): Binter/Iberia/Vueling/Canaryfly to Gran Canaria, Tenerife, Madrid, Barcelona; Condor, Eurowings, Discover, easyJet, Edelweiss, Transavia, TUI, Luxair and others to Germany, Switzerland, Benelux, Denmark, UK (Gatwick), Poland; schedules are seasonal. Ferries Santa Cruz de La Palma to Los Cristianos (Tenerife), about 2.5 h, Fred. Olsen and Naviera Armas; timetables disagree across aggregator sites. (8) Hospital General de La Palma (Breña Alta) has ICU, dialysis and the main specialties; the regional referral hospital is Hospital Universitario de Canarias (Tenerife); private options on the island were not verified. Several items above came from search snippets, not pages opened.

locales.name: La Gomera (Valle Gran Rey / San Sebastián)
locales.area: Valle Gran Rey for sun, beach and the small long-stay community; San Sebastián de La Gomera for the ferry, hospital, shops and the island's only coworking/coliving.
locales.summary: A small, steep, quiet island of about 22,000 people with a mild, dry coast, Garajonay laurel forest above it and a slow village rhythm. It suits someone who wants calm, hiking and low costs for one to three months, but it is thin on coworking, specialist medicine, flights and mid-term rentals, and everything off-island goes through Tenerife.

monthNotes.reason: San Sebastián de La Gomera (AEMET OpenData 1991-2020, 15 m): mean max 21.4-22.3 °C, min 16.2-17.3 °C, 9-22 mm and only 1.4-2.9 rain days a month, RH 67-70%. Airport station (219 m) is cooler: max about 20.6 °C in Jan/Feb. Saharan dust (calima) is most frequent Dec-Mar, so some hazy, warm days. The north-side valleys and Garajonay are cloudier and wetter than the south-west coast these ratings are for.
San Sebastián: mean max 23.3 °C (May) and 25.2 °C (Jun), min 18.6-20.3 °C, rain 1.1 and 0.5 mm, 0.3 and 0.1 rain days. Dry, warm, not yet hot; trade-wind cloud is usual on the north side.

San Sebastián: mean max 26.8 / 27.9 / 27.4 °C, min 21.8-22.7 °C, RH 70-73%, rain 0.4-2.2 mm. Warm and humid nights, and wildfire risk peaks in the dry months (the 2012 fire burned in August). Airport station (219 m) peaks at 27.3 °C max in August. Local fiestas and Spanish holiday crowds in Aug.

stay.why: Base for 1-3 months: quiet, sunny, cheap and walkable, but the island has about 22,000 people, one coworking/coliving in the capital, limited mid-term rentals and no specialist hospital. Beyond about four months the isolation and the cross-island drives (Valle Gran Rey to San Sebastián is a winding road of roughly an hour) tend to wear.

cost.note: Rent for a furnished 1-bed in Valle Gran Rey or San Sebastián (about 700-1,000), food and eating out about 600-700, a car or taxis and bus about 100-250, utilities, SIM and a coworking desk in San Sebastián about 150-250. Health insurance excluded. Rent figure is an estimate from thin listing data (see caveats).

entry.summary: Spain-wide rules. EU/EEA citizens can live and work freely (register with the foreigners' office/obtain a residence certificate after 3 months). US and UK citizens can stay 90 days in any 180 visa-free in the Schengen area (check current EES/ETIAS requirements before travel). The Spanish teleworker (digital nomad) route: a visa valid up to 1 year, or, for people already legally in Spain (including on a 90-day visa-free stay), a residence permit applied for directly in Spain, valid up to 3 years. Requirements per Spain's foreign ministry: employment or contracts with companies outside Spain (at least 3 months of relationship, to continue at least 1 year), a degree or 3 years' experience, income of 200% of the minimum wage (EUR 2,849 a month for 2026 spread over 12 months, or EUR 2,442 over the 14 statutory payments; plus EUR 916 for a first dependant and EUR 306 for each further one), no criminal record, health insurance with full public-system cover, and Spanish social-security registration. Self-employed applicants may take at most 20% of their work from Spanish clients. Not open to EU citizens. Tax residency generally arises after more than 183 days in Spain in a calendar year (general rule, not confirmed on the page opened; take tax advice).

locales.caveats: AEMET's own 1991-2020 normals table is empty for both La Gomera stations (airport C329B and San Sebastián C329Z), so the monthly figures are from the Wikipedia climate tables that cite AEMET OpenData (San Sebastián, 15 m) and the airport station (219 m, annual about 181 mm, 19.9 rain days, RH 67%); there is no official station in Valle Gran Rey. Valle Gran Rey is the drier, sunnier south-west and generally warmer in winter than the north; aggregator figures for it conflict (one gives January max 17 °C and 70 mm, which looks too cool and wet), so treat it as unmeasured. Air score: no annual PM2.5 mean was found; IQAir snapshots of 5-16 µg/m³ suggest a clean island background, and calima episodes cluster in winter (Dec-Mar) per AEMET-linked studies. Rent: no idealista/fotocasa figures could be opened (idealista blocked; Fotocasa article had no Gomera figures); RealAdvisor shows a median flat rent of about EUR 1,034 for San Sebastián (Oct 2026, range 506-2,189) and listings for mid-term furnished flats in Valle Gran Rey were not priced, so the EUR 700-1,000 rent band is an estimate. Canary law 6/2025 (published 12 Dec 2025 in the regional gazette, 23 Dec in the BOE) restricts holiday lets and sets an 80% minimum residential use in the 'green islands' including La Gomera; its effect on mid-term furnished rentals is not yet measurable and a later decree-law amended it. Housing is tight and small. Health: Hospital Nuestra Señora de Guadalupe (San Sebastián) is a small public hospital with MRI and an on-island chemotherapy unit; specialist and major care are referred to Hospital Universitario Nuestra Señora de Candelaria in Santa Cruz de Tenerife (by ferry to Los Cristianos, or by helicopter in emergencies), and a day hospital tender (EUR 1.1m) is pending. Valle Gran Rey has only a health centre and is a long road trip from the hospital. Internet: Telefónica's 2016-17 subsidised FTTH project lists Valle Gran Rey (about 33 localities) among completed deployments, with 300 Mbps symmetric advertised; WiFi Gomera advertises 1 Gbps symmetric. No measured speeds found, mobile 4G is decent in towns but weak in valleys and 5G is limited, and an island-wide power outage occurred in January 2026; test the connection before committing. Getting there: Tenerife South (TFS) is the realistic gateway, then TITSA bus 40 to Los Cristianos and a Fred. Olsen or Baleària ferry (about 50 minutes, one-way fares about EUR 40-46 in 2026; Naviera Armas was named by one aggregator, others show Baleària on the route, so check operators). La Gomera Airport (GMZ) has only Binter flights to Tenerife North and Gran Canaria (two daily each as of 2019; current schedule not confirmed), and no direct flights to mainland Spain or abroad; from San Sebastián the bus to Valle Gran Rey takes well over an hour. Bajada date for 2028 comes from one tourism listing only; confirm with the Cabildo or the Cofradía. Garajonay: the August 2012 fire burned roughly 3,000-3,600 ha (sources disagree), about 10% of the island and 18-20% of the national park; I found no 2025-26 fire reports.

locales.name: El Hierro (Valverde)
locales.area: Valverde for the hospital, shops and the island's only listed coworking; the warmer east coast (Tamaduste/airport side) or the El Golfo valley (Frontera) if you want sun and a quieter setting. A car is essential.
locales.summary: El Hierro is the smallest, quietest and least developed Canary island: a UNESCO biosphere reserve with hiking, diving at La Restinga and very mild weather in every month. It is a good place for a few focused weeks, but it is thin as a base: one small coworking, very few mid-term rentals, patchy 5G, and any serious medical care means transfer to Tenerife.

Valverde town (about 606 m) runs several degrees cooler and cloudier with the NE trades.

C929I airport: mean max 20.9 C (Jan) and 20.8 C (Feb), min 16.4-16.6 C, 28-38 mm rain over 2.7-3.1 rain days, only 145-157 sun hours. Mild but greyer; Valverde at about 600 m is cooler and often under cloud, and winter calima peaks (3-4 days) are tied to DANA lows.

C929I: warmest of the year, mean max 26.1 C (Aug) and 26.5 C (Sep), mean min 20.9-21.7 C, humidity 76-77%, 0-3 mm rain (Oct 14 mm over 2.5 rain days), 194-239 sun hours. Warm and humid rather than hot; summer calima episodes last 6-8 days and Spanish holiday crowds fill August.

C929I: mean max 23.7 C (Nov) and 22.2 C (Dec), min 17.8-19.5 C, wettest months at 37-44 mm over 3.3-4.6 rain days, and the lowest sunshine of the year (139-152 h). Still mild by European standards; upland Valverde is cooler and wetter.

stay.why: Better as a destination than a base: one small coworking open weekdays 08:30-15:30, very few long-let listings, 5G coverage below 25% in Valverde, and specialist care means a transfer to Tenerife. A self-sufficient worker with a car and a monthly rental can stay longer.

cost.note: One visit of 1-3 weeks: self-catering apartment or rural house, a rental car (essential), food and a few days at the coworking; excludes flights to the Canaries. Staying longer than about 6 weeks works out near EUR1,600-1,900 a month (about EUR600-850 for a rent that is hard to find, EUR210 coworking, car, food). This is an estimate; no nightly-rate data was verified.

entry.summary: EU/EEA citizens need no visa and can stay and work freely. US and UK passport holders get 90 days in any 180 across the whole Schengen area (the Canaries are in Schengen; EES biometric checks apply at the border). Spain's teleworking (digital nomad) visa suits remote workers for non-Spanish companies: income of at least 200% of the monthly minimum wage, a degree or 3 years of comparable experience, one-year visa validity, and a residence permit of up to 3 years if applied for from inside Spain; Spanish clients are capped at 20% of professional activity. The 183-day Spanish tax-residency rule applies. The Canaries use IGIC (7% general rate) instead of mainland VAT.

locales.caveats: Climate normals: AEMET only publishes the 1981-2010 period for Hierro Aeropuerto (C929I, 32 m), not 1991-2020; ratings use it for the east coast. Valverde town (about 606 m) has a mean near 17 C (Climates to Travel) and is cooler and cloudier, so winter days there are noticeably less pleasant than the airport figures; no AEMET highland normals were opened. The north/west (El Golfo, Frontera) was not given separate normals. Calima: the AEMET-linked material found says intense episodes cluster in winter (3-4 days) and last 6-8 days in summer, and radar work says eastern islands are hit most; no El Hierro-specific frequency was found. Air: no El Hierro annual PM2.5 figure found; IQAir gives the Canaries as a whole at about 1.4x the WHO guideline (roughly 7 ug/m3), used as a proxy. Rent: idealista and fotocasa had too few listings for an average (e.g. a furnished 1-bed finca in Valverde at EUR690, a 1-bed rural house in Mocanal at EUR560, a 2-bed flat at EUR850-1,050); seasonal lets run higher. Ley 6/2025 (in force 13 Dec 2025) limits holiday lets, but no El Hierro mid-term effect was verified. Internet: no municipality-level fibre figure found; a 2025 summary cited 5G coverage under 25% in Valverde and 48% island-wide, and the island depends on limited submarine links (a Canalink cable from Tamaduste to Tenerife is planned, no date). Health: the public Hospital Insular Nuestra Senora de los Reyes (Valverde) has 7 resident and 15 visiting outpatient specialties, a new MRI (July 2026) and an oncology clinic, but serious cases go to Tenerife (Candelaria is the reference hospital) by medical helicopter or plane; no private hospital was found. La Restinga and other ports are seeing heavy cayuco arrivals in late 2026 (a field hospital was set up at San Andres in November 2026 and emergency staff are stretched); this has not changed tourist safety in sources found, but recorded offences rose 17.4% in 2025 (Nomad Watch citing local press). Ferry (Fred. Olsen Express and Naviera Armas, Los Cristianos to La Estaca, about 2 h 20-30) and Binter schedules come from aggregators; check the operators. There are no direct international flights; connect via Tenerife Norte or Gran Canaria. Cost per trip is an estimate. Whether 24 September is also an island holiday for the Virgen de los Reyes was seen only in a snippet and is not listed above.
